title: Lending Bix his tuxedo
summary: Bix phones asking to borrow a tuxedo and rides out of town with it; days later he buys the horn.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: something about Bix. When he came into town this time to go to the Chicago Theater, we all knew that the Paul Whiteman band was coming in. And I got a 'phone call about six thirty in the morning and it was Bix on a Monday, they were supposed to open that day. And Bix says to me, hey kid, this is Bix. You know, I said, oh Bix, I know you're coming and I'm going to come down. He says, look, he says, you got a tuxedo? I said, sure. He said, well look, I left mine in Detroit and he says, bring your down I'd like to borrow it from you and I can't get a new one now. Bring it down will you?

I said, I'll be down there. He said, I've got a rehearsal at such and such a time and so I got down there early and brought the tuxedo and that's the last time I saw the tuxedo. (LAUGHTER). It didn't make any difference to me you know. But that shows how, the kind of people we were you know. So he needed a tuxedo...
He rode right on out of town with it huh?
He rode right out of town with it but...
But that's after he gave, paid
Well a few days later he bought that horn for me and I didn't even care about the tuxedo.
Oh, the tuxedo came first and then the horn came afterwards? (LAUGHTER).

That's right. Yes, but as far as blowing the horn is concerned Bix broke it in. The springs got the tension on the springs properly so that they come up real fast and so forth, strong. Now let's see, where were we?
